PLSsemLab 1.1.0 adds two analyses suggested by users.

**Necessary condition analysis (NCA) combined with PLS-SEM** (Dul, 2016; Richter et al., 2020, 2023). A new *Necessary Condition Analysis* box, with its own Run checkbox, tests every construct with a direct path to an endogenous construct as a necessary condition, on the unstandardized construct scores of the IPMA rescaled to 0-100:

- CE-FDH and CR-FDH effect sizes d with Dul's benchmarks, permutation p values (Dul, van der Laan & Kuik, 2020; 10 000 permutations by default, with the bootstrap's seed), accuracy and a verdict (necessary when d ≥ 0.1 and p < .05);
- the combined reading with the PLS-SEM paths: must-have, should-have, both or neither;
- bottleneck tables, ceiling plots, interpretation, guide and the equivalent R code.

The module computes the NCA itself: 10 000 permutations take seconds and can be cancelled. `validation/nca_equivalence.R` checks in CI that scores, effect sizes, accuracy, bottlenecks and p values (with the same permutations) equal `NCA::nca_analysis()` (135 checks, 0 failed).

**Measurement invariance of the reflective constructs as common factors.** In the *Multigroup Analysis* box, a multigroup CFA with lavaan (configural, metric and scalar; MLR by default) next to MICOM, with the chi-square difference and the changes in CFI, RMSEA and SRMR judged by Chen's (2007) limits. The configural model is judged by CFI and SRMR, and the report explains why RMSEA does not decide when it has few degrees of freedom (Kenny, Kaniskan & McCoach, 2015).

The attached `.jmo` is built for jamovi 2.7.41 on Windows (R 4.5.0). Changes: see `NEWS.md`.
